text:
---
name: rfe.speedrun
description: End-to-end RFE pipeline. Accepts an idea, Jira key(s), or a YAML batch file. Creates, reviews, auto-fixes (with splits), and submits. Supports --headless, --announce-complete, --dry-run. Use when taking a problem statement all the way to a submitted RFE in one run.
user-invocable: true
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, AskUserQuestion, Skill
---

You are running the full RFE pipeline in speedrun mode. Your goal is to go from problem statements to submitted Jira tickets with minimal interaction. You orchestrate by calling other skills — never duplicate their work.

## Step 0: Parse Arguments and Persist Flags

Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for:
- `--input <path>`: Path to a YAML file with batch entries
- `--headless`: Suppress questions and confirmations (for CI / eval)
- `--announce-complete`: Print completion marker when done (for CI / eval harnesses)
- `--dry-run`: Skip Jira writes in submit
- `--batch-size N`: Override batch size (default 5), passed to auto-fix
- Remaining arguments: either a single Jira key (RHAIRFE-NNNN) or a free-text idea

Clean temp state and persist parsed flags. `batch_size` MUST be a concrete integer — with no `--batch-size`, write the speedrun default `5`, never `<N>` or `null`.

```bash
python3 scripts/state.py clean
python3 scripts/prep_assess.py --clean-all
python3 scripts/state.py init tmp/speedrun-config.yaml headless=<true/false> announce_complete=<true/false> dry_run=<true/false> batch_size=<N or 5> input_file=<path or null>
```

Determine pipeline mode:
- **Mode A (Batch YAML)**: `--input` flag present → batch create + auto-fix + submit
- **Mode B (Existing RFE)**: argument is a Jira key (RHAIRFE-NNNN) → skip create, auto-fix + submit
- **Mode C (Single idea)**: free-text argument, no `--input` → single create + auto-fix + submit

If no arguments provided, stop with usage instructions.

## Step 0.5: Bootstrap Dependencies

Run bootstrap early so agent definitions (e.g. `rfe-scorer`) land in
`.claude/agents/` before Phase 2 needs them; the CREATE phase gives the rescan
time to register them.

```bash
bash scripts/bootstrap-assess-rfe.sh
```

If bootstrap fails, retry once, then continue — auto-fix bootstraps again in its own setup step.

## Defaults

Unless specified: priority Normal, size S/M, no labels, one RFE per entry (more only if an entry holds several distinct business needs).

## Phase 1: Create

**Mode A (Batch YAML)**: Read the YAML input file. Format:

```yaml
- prompt: "Users need to verify model signatures at serving time"
  priority: Critical
  labels: [candidate-3.5]
  clarifying_context: |
    Customers: Crestview Investments, DataPulse.
    Business justification: $4.2M renewal at risk; 3 escalations in Q3.
- prompt: "TrustyAI operator crashes on large clusters"
  priority: Major
```

`clarifying_context` is optional, but when an entry has one it holds the ONLY copy of
the requester's business evidence — named accounts, figures, the user problem, scope
and success criteria. WHY is scored on that evidence. **Forward it verbatim to
`/rfe.create`. Never summarise it and never drop it** — an entry launched without it
produces an RFE that says no customer evidence was supplied, which costs WHY a full
point on every RFE in the batch.

Validate before spending agent budget. `--strict` makes unknown fields and duplicate prompts (usually typos) block the run too, not just hard errors:

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_batch_input.py <input_file> --strict
```

Nonzero exit: stop and report the printed `ERROR:`/`WARNING:` lines — never fan out agents against a batch already known to be malformed.

Count entries and pre-allocate all IDs upfront:

```bash
python3 scripts/next_rfe_id.py --from-batch <input_file>   # input_file = the --input path; prints one RFE ID per entry
```

Persist the pre-allocated IDs before launching any agents — the Phase 1 barrier below reads this file:

```bash
python3 scripts/state.py write-ids tmp/speedrun-all-ids.txt <all_IDs>
```

For each entry, launch an Agent to invoke `/rfe.create`. Pass the pre-assigned ID so each Agent knows which ID to use, and append the entry's `clarifying_context` as a labelled block:

```
Agent(prompt: "/rfe.create --headless --rfe-id RFE-<N> [--priority <priority>] <prompt>

Clarifying context from the requester (verbatim — this is the evidence for ## Affected Customers and ## Business Justification):
<clarifying_context>")
```

Worked example for entry 1 of the batch above:

```
Agent(prompt: "/rfe.create --headless --rfe-id RFE-001 --priority Critical Users need to verify model signatures at serving time

Clarifying context from the requester (verbatim — this is the evidence for ## Affected Customers and ## Business Justification):
Customers: Crestview Investments, DataPulse.
Business justification: $4.2M renewal at risk; 3 escalations in Q3.")
```

If an entry has no `clarifying_context`, omit the whole block — never emit the header with nothing under it.

Each entry is one business need — `/rfe.create` must produce exactly one RFE per invocation. Launch all N Agents in one message so they run concurrently. Your next Bash call after that message MUST be the Phase 1 barrier — a blocking check that reads the task files on disk:

```bash
python3 scripts/check_review_progress.py --wait --phase create --id-file tmp/speedrun-all-ids.txt
```

Call it immediately, before any agent has reported. The barrier is the ONLY completion signal for Phase 1 — never count agent-completion notifications.

Exit 0 = all N task files exist with parseable frontmatter carrying their own `rfe_id`; Phase 1 is done. Exit 3 = timeout, not failure; it prints the still-pending IDs (a half-written or wrong-`rfe_id` file counts as pending). Re-run while that list keeps shrinking. If the same IDs stay pending across 3 consecutive exit-3 results, those agents are dead — launch a replacement Agent for each, then resume the barrier. You need exactly N IDs before moving on. **Never delete or re-create task files during Phase 1** — quality is Phase 2's job.

**Mode B (Existing RFE)**: Skip Phase 1. The Jira key(s) from arguments become the processing list.

**Mode C (Single idea)**: Invoke `/rfe.create` with the user's input:

```
/rfe.create [--headless] <idea_text>
```

If not headless, `/rfe.create` asks clarifying questions. Collect created RFE IDs.

After Phase 1 (all modes), persist the ID list to disk:

```bash
python3 scripts/state.py write-ids tmp/speedrun-all-ids.txt <all_IDs>
```

## Phase 2: Auto-fix

Re-read config and ID list from disk (in case context was compressed during Phase 1):

```bash
python3 scripts/state.py read tmp/speedrun-config.yaml
python3 scripts/state.py read-ids tmp/speedrun-all-ids.txt
```

Invoke auto-fix with the **Skill** tool (NOT Agent — Agent runs in background and terminates the session). Build the args from the config file:

```
Skill(skill: "rfe.auto-fix", args: "--headless --announce-complete --batch-size <batch_size> <all_IDs_from_file>")
```

Pass `--headless` and `--announce-complete` through if set in the config. **Always** pass `--batch-size <batch_size>` from `tmp/speedrun-config.yaml` — never omit it and never let auto-fix's default take over.

Auto-fix handles assessment, feasibility, review, auto-revision, re-assessment, splits, retries and the run report. The Skill call blocks until it completes — this is correct. **Do NOT stop, summarize, or skip remaining batches early**; every ID must go through all phases. Never end a turn with a text-only response in order to wait for something — that hands control back.

**Bash discipline:** never use command substitution `$(...)` or chain with `;`, `&&`, `||` — they trigger an approval prompt and are denied in headless mode. To pass a value between commands, write it to a `tmp/` file with `scripts/state.py` and read it back.

After auto-fix returns, verify all RFEs were processed:

```bash
python3 scripts/check_autofix_complete.py
```

On exit 1 the output shows `MISSING_IDS=RFE-006,RFE-007,...`. Re-invoke auto-fix with only those IDs:

```
Skill(skill: "rfe.auto-fix", args: "--headless --batch-size <batch_size> <missing_IDs>")
```

Repeat verify+retry until all RFEs have reviews or 3 retries are exhausted.

## Phase 3: Submit

Re-read flags and IDs from disk (context may have been compressed), then collect passing IDs:

```bash
python3 scripts/state.py read tmp/speedrun-config.yaml
python3 scripts/state.py read-ids tmp/speedrun-all-ids.txt
python3 scripts/collect_recommendations.py <all_IDs_from_file>
```

Parse the `SUBMIT=` line. If no IDs are ready to submit, skip to Phase 4. Otherwise invoke submit using the **Skill** tool:

```
Skill(skill: "rfe.submit", args: "--dry-run --headless <passing_IDs>")
```

Pass `--dry-run` and `--headless` through if set in the config. If not headless, `/rfe.submit` shows a confirmation table before writing to Jira — the one mandatory interaction point.

## Phase 4: Summary

Re-read flags:

```bash
python3 scripts/state.py read tmp/speedrun-config.yaml
```

If headless, output a brief machine-readable summary. If interactive, output a
`## Speedrun Complete` section with: each created RFE (ID, title, priority); review
counts (passed / failed / split into N children); each submitted key with
created/updated/dry-run; the run report and HTML report paths under
`artifacts/auto-fix-runs/`; and any RFE that could not be auto-fixed (or "None").

$ARGUMENTS
